hypothesis: A minimal ISA v0 core (fetch/decode/execute, 4 registers, GPIO bus on uio[7:0], WAIT/branch/DECJNZ) can be implemented and differentially verified against an independent Python model within the Tiny Tapeout cmos5l template.
baseline: No RTL existed; repository contained only planning documents.
change: Added src/{project,core,alu,gpio,program_rom}.v, tools/{assembler,isa_model}.py, firmware/loop_demo.asm, test/test.py (differential cocotb test). Toolchain: Miniforge/conda-forge (iverilog 13.0, verilator 5.052, yosys 0.69, cocotb 2.0.1) installed without sudo.
result: Two bugs found and fixed during bring-up: (1) markdown-style backticks and a literal "*/" substring inside Verilog block comments caused Icarus preprocessor/parser errors (backticks are macro-expanded even inside comments; "GDIR*/GWR*" prematurely closed a block comment) - fixed by removing backticks/'*/' from all RTL comments. (2) A genuine RTL bug: `rd_val`/`rs_val` were continuous assignments driven by a function (`reg_read`) that read module-level regs (r0-r3) not in its argument list; Icarus only tracked the explicit argument (rd_idx) for re-evaluation, so back-to-back instructions targeting the same register (ANDI R0 -> ORI R0 -> XORI R0) read a stale value. Fixed by replacing the function call with explicit continuous-assign muxes. Also fixed a cocotb testbench issue (not an RTL bug): reading DUT-internal registers immediately after `await RisingEdge` raced with the DUT's own NBA updates; fixed with `await ReadOnly()` after each RisingEdge before sampling.
tests: test/test.py::test_isa_v0_differential (cocotb, Icarus Verilog): assembles firmware/loop_demo.asm, runs it on both RTL and tools/isa_model.py, asserts pc/r0-r3/z/halted/uio_oe/uio_out match every cycle.
outcome: PASS - 50 cycles, RTL matches Python model exactly, program reaches HALT.

hypothesis: The chip can be made genuinely reprogrammable after fabrication by adding a serial bootloader FSM (over the existing uio bus, no new pins) that writes a real program RAM, replacing the $readmemh-fixed ROM; ISA v1 also needs SHIFTOUT/SHIFTIN for byte-oriented firmware.
baseline: ISA v0: src/program_rom.v ($readmemh, fixed at elaboration), 19 opcodes, no shift instructions.
change: Added src/program_ram.v (writable), a bootloader FSM in src/core.v (LD_WAIT/LD_COUNT/LD_WORD/LD_DONE states) driven over uio[0:2] (LOAD_REQ/LOAD_CLK/LOAD_DATA), SHIFTOUT/SHIFTIN opcodes (19,20), test/bootload.py (cocotb driver for the protocol), and migrated the existing differential test off $readmemh entirely onto the bootloader path.
result: Two timing bugs found and fixed during bring-up: (1) the GPIO input synchronizer resets to 0 and takes 2 cycles to reflect the real external pin value, so sampling LOAD_REQ on the very first post-reset cycle always read 0 regardless of what the host drove - fixed with an explicit 2-cycle settle counter before the bootloader's first sample. (2) the cocotb bootloader driver hands off to normal execution mid-way through its final bit-clock pulse (the FSM transitions to LD_DONE partway through the driver's own trailing awaits), so a naive test setup assuming PC=0 immediately after the driver returns was wrong (observed PC=4 instead of the expected 1); fixed by snapshotting the RTL's actual post-load architectural state (pc/r0-r3/z/halted/wait_remaining/gpio_dir/gpio_out) into the Python model instead of assuming a fixed handoff cycle count.
tests: test/test.py::test_isa_v1_differential (cocotb, Icarus Verilog): loads firmware/loop_demo.asm (now exercising SHIFTOUT/SHIFTIN too) purely via test/bootload.py's serial protocol (no $readmemh anywhere), then differentially compares RTL against tools/isa_model.py every cycle.
outcome: PASS - 63 cycles, RTL matches Python model exactly, program reaches HALT, loaded entirely through the new bootloader mechanism.

hypothesis: Real protocol bit-banging (UART TX) can be generated by parameterized assembly and verified on RTL against an independent asynchronous UART receiver model across edge-case data and multiple bit periods, alongside isolated unit tests for all individual opcodes.
baseline: Iteration 1: Only loop_demo.asm exercised indirectly, no protocol firmware, no independent protocol decoders.
change: Added tools/uart_model.py (UartReceiver independent decoder + build_uart_tx_asm parameterized generator), test/test_uart.py (tests 0x00, 0xFF, 0x55, 0xAA and pseudorandom bytes at 4, 8, 16 cycles/bit each with fresh reset/bootload), test/test_opcodes.py (isolated unit tests for ALU, registers, branches, loops, GPIO, shifts), and added both to COCOTB_TEST_MODULES.
result: All 6 test suites pass cleanly. Derived cycle-exact timing: SHIFTOUT takes 1 cycle to drive uio_out, so WAIT (P-2) gives exactly P cycles per bit. Identified UART RX quantization jitter (3 cycles on GRD/ANDI/JNZ loop causing 37.5%-75% phase error at P<=8) motivating Iteration 3 WAITEDGE hardware primitive.
tests: scripts/regress.sh running test, test_uart, test_opcodes: 6 suites, 0 failures, 5.26ms sim time.
outcome: PASS - All UART edge cases, pseudorandom sequences, and per-opcode unit tests passed on RTL.

hypothesis: An RVFI-inspired trace interface (PVFI) and SymbiYosys formal harness (BMC via Z3) can formally verify safety invariants (reset convergence, PC bounds, WAIT countdown, halt permanence, counter monotonicity), while a dedicated WAITEDGE edge-capture instruction enables single-cycle accurate pulse width and autobaud measurement without software polling jitter.
baseline: Iteration 2: 21 opcodes, no formal harness or trace interface; pulse/baud measurement restricted to 3-cycle jittered polling loop.
change: Added OP_WAITEDGE (opcode 21) with 32-bit hardware cycle counter (cycle_cnt) and edge_wait_cnt in src/core.v; PVFI trace interface ports gated under `ifdef PVFI with zero silicon overhead; SymbiYosys formal harness in formal/core.sby and formal/core_formal.v proving core safety invariants over 20 steps with Z3; test/test_waitedge.py testing pulse width measurement (5, 11, 23, 47 cycles), free-running timestamp capture, and cycle-by-cycle differential match.
result: SymbiYosys formal BMC passed 20 steps with 0 violations. All 9 cocotb regression tests passed. Single-cycle precision pulse width measurement verified for 5, 11, 23, 47 cycles without polling jitter.
tests: formal/core.sby (SBY/Z3 20-step BMC PASS); scripts/regress.sh (9/9 cocotb tests PASS: pulse measurement, timestamp capture, differential).
outcome: PASS - Formal safety proofs and WAITEDGE timing discovery fully verified.

hypothesis: Empirical bug detection power can be quantified via seeded RTL mutation testing, unexpected corner cases can be explored by a constrained-random instruction fuzzer with automated delta-debugging shrinking, and real PPA can be measured via standard cell synthesis in Yosys.
baseline: Iteration 3: 9 tests, 22 opcodes, no mutation testing, no randomized fuzzer, placeholder PPA figures in docs/ppa.md.
change: Added scripts/mutate.py with 10 seeded architectural mutation operators covering all RTL modules; built tools/fuzzer.py and test/test_fuzz.py with 10 differential random execution runs and automated delta-debugging shrinking; established real synthesis baseline via scripts/synth.sh and scripts/synth.ys targeting generic CMOS/IHP 130nm.
result: Mutation testing achieved 10/10 killed (100.0% kill rate) in 46.95s. Fuzzer executed 10 full random programs differentially with 0 mismatches, and shrinker unit test verified minimal counterexample extraction. Yosys synthesis measured 14,056 pre-mapping cells, 19,143 mapped CMOS gates, 37,542 GE, revealing that 92.7% of design area is the synthesized 4096-bit RAM matrix while the processor core occupies only 1,402 cells (~1.99 kGE).
tests: scripts/mutate.py (10/10 KILLED, 100% kill rate); scripts/regress.sh (11/11 PASS); scripts/synth.sh (synthesis complete, zero design problems).
outcome: PASS - Full verification hardening and real PPA baseline established.

hypothesis: The core can execute full-duplex SPI Master communications across all 4 standard modes (CPOL 0/1, CPHA 0/1) by upgrading SHIFTOUT/SHIFTIN with an MSB shift-direction flag in operand[3], verified against an independent software SPI slave model.
baseline: Iteration 4: 11 tests, UART only protocol firmware, SHIFTOUT/SHIFTIN restricted to LSB-first shifts.
change: Upgraded src/core.v, tools/assembler.py, tools/isa_model.py so operand[3] selects MSB-first vs LSB-first shift direction; implemented tools/spi_model.py (build_spi_master_asm + SpiSlave independent state machine); created test/test_spi.py exercising Mode 0, Mode 1, Mode 2, Mode 3, full-duplex simultaneous MISO/MOSI transfer, edge cases, and random bytes; updated PVFI trace mapping.
result: All 14 tests pass cleanly. SpiSlave received all transmitted bytes across all 4 modes without framing or phase errors. Full-duplex bidirectional transfer verified Master RX captured 0x42 while Slave RX captured 0x7E. SymbiYosys 20-step formal proof passed. Yosys synthesis added only 41 cells (19,184 total mapped cells).
tests: scripts/regress.sh (14/14 cocotb PASS); sby -f formal/core.sby (Z3 20-step BMC PASS); scripts/mutate.py (10/10 KILLED, 100% kill rate); scripts/synth.sh (PASS).
outcome: PASS - Complete 4-mode SPI Master and full-duplex protocol capability verified.

hypothesis: True I2C bus compliance and contention elimination can be achieved in silicon by adding hardware open-drain primitives (OP_GODRI, OP_GODR), enabling single-instruction open-drain masking where writing 0 drives low and writing 1 releases the line to input/pullup, verified by a cycle-accurate I2cSlave model and electrical contention checks.
baseline: Iteration 5: 14 tests, push-pull GPIO only, open-drain bus operations required manual pin direction reconfiguration risking shoot-through bus contention.
change: Added OP_GODRI (opcode 22) and OP_GODR (opcode 23) in src/core.v and tools/{assembler,isa_model}.py; added hardware open-drain tri-state gating in src/gpio.v; implemented tools/i2c_model.py (build_i2c_write_asm, build_i2c_read_asm using compact DECJNZ loops, and independent I2cSlave state machine); created test/test_i2c.py with 5 comprehensive cocotb test cases; added formal contention prevention invariant assert((uio_oe & gpio_od_mode & uio_out) == 8'h00) in formal harness; added MUT_11 open-drain fault operator in scripts/mutate.py.
result: All 19 regression tests passed (100%). Single-byte write, multi-byte EEPROM write, single-byte read with Master NACK, unresponsive slave NACK detection, and cycle-by-cycle electrical contention safety all verified. SymbiYosys proved the open-drain safety invariant over 20 steps (0 violations). Mutation testing achieved 11/11 killed (100.0% kill rate). Yosys synthesis mapped 19,243 CMOS cells (+59 cells over baseline, active core logic is 1,486 cells, ~2.1 kGE).
tests: scripts/regress.sh (19/19 cocotb PASS); sby -f formal/core.sby (Z3 20-step BMC PASS); scripts/mutate.py (11/11 KILLED, 100% kill rate); scripts/synth.sh (19,243 cells, zero latches).
outcome: PASS - Hardware open-drain and verified I2C Master protocol engine complete.

hypothesis: I2C slave clock stretching can be dynamically synchronized and measured in software using hardware WAITEDGE without polling jitter, and multi-master bus arbitration loss can be detected cycle-by-cycle via GRD line verification to abort collisions safely.
baseline: Iteration 6: I2C write/read firmware assumed ideal zero-stretch slaves and single-master bus topology without arbitration detection.
change: Added build_i2c_write_with_stretch_asm() in tools/i2c_model.py utilizing WAITEDGE R3, 0x09 to synchronize on slave SCL release and capture stretch duration; added build_i2c_write_with_arbitration_asm() with per-bit GRD line verification on driven 1s with atomic bus release (GWRI 0xFF) and error exit code 0xEE on collision; updated I2cSlave model to simulate configurable clock_stretch_cycles; added test_i2c_clock_stretching, test_i2c_arbitration_loss_detection, and test_i2c_arbitration_win_normal in test/test_i2c.py.
result: All 22 regression tests passed (100%). Clock stretching test verified 20-cycle slave stretch was absorbed cleanly, with WAITEDGE capturing 15 remaining wait cycles into R3 without timing corruption. Arbitration loss test verified immediate detection of external bus contention, instant bus release, and 0xEE return code. Clean arbitration win verified normal completion with 0x00. SymbiYosys 20-step formal proof passed (0 violations). Mutation testing achieved 11/11 mutants killed (100.0% kill rate). Synthesis cell count remained unchanged at 19,243 CMOS cells (pure firmware and verification expansion with 0 additional silicon area).
tests: scripts/regress.sh (22/22 cocotb PASS); sby -f formal/core.sby (Z3 20-step BMC PASS); scripts/mutate.py (11/11 KILLED, 100.0% kill rate); scripts/synth.sh (19,243 cells, zero timing/area overhead).
outcome: PASS - I2C clock stretching synchronization and multi-master arbitration loss detection verified.

hypothesis: On-chip hardware CRC-8 calculation (poly 0x07) can protect the serial bootloader against corrupted, noisy, or truncated load frames, reporting load success/error on uo_out[1:0] and permanently halting execution on error to eliminate execution of invalid machine code.
baseline: Iteration 7: 22 tests, bootloader frame had no integrity check or error signaling; corrupted/truncated loads ran whatever random bits remained in RAM.
change: Added 8-bit CRC-8 accumulator (poly 0x07, x^8 + x^2 + x + 1, init 0x00) and LD_CRC state in src/core.v; exposed boot_done (uo_out[0]) and boot_err (uo_out[1]) on chip dedicated outputs in src/project.v; added formal invariant in formal/core_formal.v proving assert(pvfi_halted && !pvfi_valid) on boot_err; updated test/bootload.py to compute and transmit CRC-8; added test/test_bootload.py with 5 comprehensive test cases (valid CRC, inverted CRC rejection, single-bit payload corruption, truncated frame abort, warm boot skip); added MUT_12_BOOTLOADER_CRC_BYPASS in scripts/mutate.py.
result: All 27 regression tests passed (100%). Clean load verified uo_out=0x01 and correct execution. Inverted CRC verified uo_out=0x03, halted=1, and PC=0. Single-bit corrupted payload verified uo_out=0x03. Premature LOAD_REQ drop verified uo_out=0x03. Warm boot skip verified uo_out=0x01. SymbiYosys proved the integrity invariant over 20 steps (0 violations). Mutation testing achieved 12/12 mutants killed (100.0% kill rate) in 180.59s. Yosys synthesis added only 48 cells (19,291 mapped cells, 37,832 GE total; active core logic is 1,580 cells, ~2.2 kGE).
tests: scripts/regress.sh (27/27 cocotb PASS); sby -f formal/core.sby (Z3 20-step BMC PASS); scripts/mutate.py (12/12 KILLED, 100.0% kill rate); scripts/synth.sh (19,291 cells, +48 cells).
outcome: PASS - Hardware CRC-8 integrity checking and error reporting fully verified.

hypothesis: Hardware edge synchronization via WAITEDGE allows bit-banged UART RX firmware to eliminate the 3-cycle software polling quantization jitter, achieving cycle-exact mid-bit sampling, framing error detection, and false-start noise glitch rejection verified against an independent transmitter model.
baseline: Iteration 8: 27 tests, UART TX only; UART RX documented as an open limitation due to 3-cycle quantization jitter on software polling loops.
change: Implemented build_uart_rx_asm(bit_period_cycles, pin, check_false_start) in tools/uart_model.py utilizing WAITEDGE R3, pin for zero-jitter start bit falling edge detection, WAIT and SHIFTIN for exact 1.5P, 2.5P..8.5P mid-bit sampling, and GRD/ANDI/JNZ for 9.5P stop bit verification; created UartTransmitter model with support for valid frames, framing errors, and false-start glitches; added 4 new cocotb test cases in test/test_uart.py (test_uart_rx_edge_cases, test_uart_rx_pseudorandom, test_uart_rx_framing_error, test_uart_rx_glitch_rejection); added MUT_13_SHIFTIN_BIT_ORDER in scripts/mutate.py.
result: All 31 regression tests passed (100%). Reception of 0x00, 0xFF, 0x55, 0xAA and pseudorandom bytes verified at periods 8 and 16 with zero bit errors. Framing error detection (stop bit held low) cleanly detected and reported 0xFE in R2. False-start noise glitch (1-cycle low pulse) cleanly rejected and reported 0xFF in R2. SymbiYosys 20-step formal proof passed with 0 violations. Mutation testing achieved 13/13 mutants killed (100.0% kill rate) in 220.45s. Zero additional silicon gates required (pure firmware & verification hardening, 19,291 CMOS cells).
tests: scripts/regress.sh (31/31 cocotb PASS); sby -f formal/core.sby (Z3 20-step BMC PASS); scripts/mutate.py (13/13 KILLED, 100.0% kill rate); scripts/synth.sh (19,291 cells, zero area overhead).
outcome: PASS - Zero-jitter UART RX with framing error handling and glitch rejection fully verified.
